info.name: ai-chat backend
info.description:
Manual test collection for the ai-chat Go backend. Set AI_CHAT_FAKE_MODE=true in your .env before starting the server to test the full pipeline (generation, events, WebSocket) with ZERO Anthropic API calls / zero token cost — every generation returns a canned no-op result almost instantly (see AI_CHAT_FAKE_DELAY_SECONDS, default 5s, to simulate latency).

Auth: every REST route forwards your bearer token to FLOWPOS_API_BASE/user for verification — there is no local auth. Set {{bearer_token}} to a real FlowPOS token. The WebSocket route authenticates differently (see the Stream request) since browsers can't set an Authorization header on a WS handshake.

item.name: Get chat (transcript + generation status)
item.description: generating:true means a background generation is running for this chat right now — poll this after Send Message if you're not using the WebSocket, or just to sanity-check state. This route is NOT removed (it's the initial page load / post-done refetch) — only /chat/status was removed.

item.name: Send message (starts a generation)
item.description: Returns 202 immediately with the recorded user message — the actual generation runs in the background. Open the Stream WebSocket request BEFORE or AFTER sending this; with fake mode + the fix, the socket stays open and will deliver this generation's events either way. Response body includes chat.id — copy it into {{chat_id}}.

item.name: Stream generation events
item.description:
IMPORTANT: Postman's native WebSocket request type (a separate top-level request type in Postman, not achievable inside a normal HTTP item) is what you actually want here — this HTTP item is a placeholder because collection JSON can't declare a ws request outside Postman's own UI action "New > WebSocket Request". Steps:

1. In Postman: New -> WebSocket Request.
2. URL: ws://localhost:8080/api/v1/chats/{{chat_id}}/stream?last_seq=0  (use wss:// against a deployed HTTPS host).
3. Go to the request's "Headers" tab (Postman's WS UI lets you set handshake headers) and add:
     Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: bearer.<BASE64URL_OF_YOUR_TOKEN>, tenant.<TENANT_ID>
   The bearer segment is base64url (RFC4648 no-padding) of your RAW bearer token, NOT base64-of-"Bearer x". Example to generate it:
     printf '%s' 'your-raw-token' | basenc --base64url | tr -d '='
   or in Node: Buffer.from('your-raw-token').toString('base64url')
4. Connect. If the fix is working you will see a 101 response and — check the response headers Postman shows for the handshake — Sec-WebSocket-Protocol echoed back with the exact same bearer.<...> value you sent. If that header is MISSING on the 101, that's the item-1 bug again (browsers would kill the connection here; Postman's WS client is lenient so it will still show you frames even if this header is absent — the header presence is what to check manually).
5. You should immediately receive: {"type":"ready","last_seq":0} (or whatever last_seq applies) — this frame alone proves the transport is healthy with NO generation running yet.
6. Fire "Send message" (REST folder) with AI_CHAT_FAKE_MODE=true on the server — no Claude call happens, but a real generation row + real events are produced. Watch this same open socket receive, in order: {"type":"started",...} -> {"type":"checking",...} -> {"type":"done",...}.
7. Confirm the socket does NOT close after "done" — send a second message and confirm its events arrive on the SAME connection without reconnecting. That is the item-4 regression check.
8. Kill the server process (or just wait) to check the ping: every 30s you should see a WS ping frame (Postman shows this in the ws frame log) keeping the connection alive with no events.
